directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis, allowing plenty of airflow through the canopy. Herbemont is a historic wine grape dating to the early 1800s in South Carolina, one of the older American hybrid grapes still valued today for its strong tolerance of Pierce's disease, the bacterial infection that has limited European wine grape production across the humid South for two centuries. It produces small, dark, sweet-tart berries used historically and still today for wine, offering a taste of the region's viticultural history along with genuine disease resilience that many modern hybrids still aim to match. Prune hard each winter to renewal spurs on permanent cordons, and thin crowded clusters in early summer to improve fruit quality and airflow.

common_name: Norton Grape (Cynthiana, Flagship Ozark Native American Red Wine Grape)

planting.note: Plant dormant, rooted vines in early spring on a sturdy trellis in well-drained soil; Norton, also sold as Cynthiana, is a native American red wine grape with exceptional disease resistance, historically the flagship red wine grape of the Ozark and Missouri wine industry.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun on a sturdy trellis, allowing plenty of airflow through the vigorous canopy. Norton, also sold under the name Cynthiana, is a pure native American grape (Vitis aestivalis) with exceptional resistance to Pierce's disease, black rot, and other diseases that limit many other wine grapes across the humid South and lower Midwest, and it served historically as the flagship red wine grape of the Ozark and Missouri wine industry before Prohibition. It produces small, dark, high-acid berries that make deeply colored, full-bodied red wine, though the fruit is generally considered too tart and seedy for fresh eating. Prune hard each winter to renewal spurs on permanent cordons, since Norton is a vigorous grower that needs regular canopy management to keep fruit quality high.
